text: For an n-qubit density operator rho, the source defines robustness of magic as the minimum sum of absolute coefficients over all signed decompositions rho=sum_i x_i sigma_i into pure n-qubit stabilizer states.
A trace-preserving stabilizer channel maps each pure stabilizer state to a convex mixture of pure stabilizer states.

Full n-qubit RoM is the minimum l1 norm of a signed affine decomposition over pure stabilizer states; trace one forces the coefficients to sum to one, and the normalization gives every free mixed stabilizer state value one.

logical_form.conclusion: R(rho)=min{sum_i |x_i| : rho=sum_i x_i sigma_i, sigma_i pure stabilizer}

text: Under the full stabilizer-polytope convention, R(rho)=1 exactly when rho lies in STAB_n, and R(rho)>1 otherwise.

For every trace-preserving stabilizer channel E that maps each pure stabilizer atom into STAB_n, full RoM satisfies R(E(rho))<=R(rho). The kernel-checked normalized scope is an exact deterministic density map equipped with atom-image convex witnesses; source protocol/channel syntax to that interface remains a separate semantic obligation.
